claims.text: Homogenized Al0.7CoCrFeNi has a dual-phase FCC/B2 lamellar structure.
The initial FCC/B2 interfaces are incoherent.
The initial alloy has high strength but low ductility.
Stress concentration and strain localization at the phase interfaces cause the low ductility and interfacial cracking.
Treatment at 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours will topologically transform the lamellae into a hierarchical pattern.
The HPHT treatment will replace incoherent FCC/B2 interfaces with coherent interfaces.
High pressure and temperature enhance diffusion and atomic rearrangement in this alloy.
Stress-driven interface migration drives the proposed topological transformation.
The transformation reduces interfacial energy and FCC/B2 misfit strain.
Coherent interfaces permit dislocations to transfer across phase boundaries instead of piling up.
The transformed structure will simultaneously activate dislocation slip, stacking faults, and twinning.
Dislocation transfer and the multiple deformation modes will homogenize strain between the FCC and B2 phases.
Homogeneous strain distribution will arrest interfacial cracking and reduce microcrack density.
The HPHT-generated microstructure will overcome the strength-ductility trade-off.
The treated alloy will have uniform elongation greater than 25%, compared with less than 15% for the baseline.
The treated alloy will have an ultimate tensile strength greater than 1.5 GPa.
The treated alloy's fracture surfaces will show elongated cracks rather than isolated microcracks.
The GND densities of the FCC and B2 phases will converge at high strain.
The untreated baseline has high GND-density gradients between the FCC and B2 phases.
Conditions above the proposed processing window may cause B2 decomposition, melting, or formation of undesirable intermetallic phases.

contradictions.description: The mechanism predicts arrested interfacial cracking and reduced microcrack density, whereas the predicted fracture morphology emphasizes elongated cracks. Elongated or coalesced cracks ordinarily indicate crack propagation, and the cited W2054455822 record specifically associates long cracks along lamellar interfaces with stress accumulation and strain localization.
